I ended up losing almost all of the baby weight (except what I needed to retain in order to not become underweight like I was before having kids!). I'm in my thirties now and more fit than I was through my 20s. Fitness is a huge part of my life now and belly dance is what started it all.

I hope that she has the same experience I did - that learning to dance will inspire her to take better care of herself all around, and that she will lose the weight. I still dance, and let me tell you, you dance better when you're thin and strong and fit than you do when you're soft and flubby. It looks a hell of a lot better too. And her teacher is wrong to tell her that you don't need core strength...haha what? Yes you do! Not only will having a strong core make it easier to balance - belly dance is traditionally done mostly in releve, on the balls of your feet - but also a lot of your movements are meant to be powered by your abdominals and your obliques. Some of it is powered by your glutes and quads, or your calves, but a huge amount of your stamina, range of motion, and precision depend on having strong core muscles. If you're doing it right you will naturally end up with abs that are strong and supple.
